messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Usual Adult Metformin Dose for Diabetes Type 2:
Immediate-release tablets:
Initial dose: 500 mg orally twice a day or 850 mg orally once a day Dose titration: Increase by 500 mg increments weekly or 850 mg every 2 weeks as tolerated. Maintenance dose: 2000 mg/day in divided doses Maximum dose: 2550 mg/day. Doses above 2,000 mg may be better tolerated given 3 times
Extended-release tablets:
Initial dose: 500 to 1000 mg orally once a day Dose titration: Increase in 500 mg increments weekly as tolerated Maximum dose: 2000 mg/day
Usual Pediatric Dose for Diabetes Type 2 (10 years or older):
Immediate-release tablets:
Initial dose: 500 mg orally twice a day Dose titration: Increase in 500 mg increments weekly as tolerated; daily dose should be taken in divided doses 2 to 3 times a day with meals Maximum dose: 2000 mg/day
Extended-release oral suspension:
Initial dose: 500 mg orally once a day with evening meal Dose titration: Increase in 500 mg increments weekly based on glycemic control and tolerability Maximum dose: 2000 mg/day
Renal Impairment:
Triples: [["metformin", "has initial dose", "500 mg orally twice a day"], ["metformin", "has initial dose", "850 mg orally once a day"], ["metformin", "has dose titration", "increase by 500 mg weekly"], ["metformin", "has dose titration", "increase by 850 mg every 2 weeks"], ["metformin", "has maintenance dose", "2000 mg/day in divided doses"], ["metformin", "has maximum dose", "2550 mg/day"], ["metformin", "has alternative dosing for doses above 2000 mg", "given 3 times"], ["metformin", "has initial dose", "500 to 1000 mg orally once a day"], ["metformin", "has maximum dose", "2000 mg/day"], ["metformin", "has initial dose for pediatric patients", "500 mg orally twice a day"], ["metformin", "has dose titration for pediatric patients", "increase by 500 mg weekly"], ["metformin", "has daily dose for pediatric patients", "divided into 2 to 3 doses with meals"], ["metformin", "has maximum dose for pediatric patients", "2000 mg/day"], ["metformin", "has initial dose for extended release suspension", "500 mg orally once a day with evening meal"], ["metformin", "has dose titration for extended release suspension", "increase by 500 mg weekly based on glycemic control and tolerability"], ["metformin", "has maximum dose for extended release suspension", "2000 mg/day"]]
Relations: ["has alternative dosing for doses above 2000 mg", "has daily dose for pediatric patients", "has dose titration", "has dose titration for extended release suspension", "has dose titration for pediatric patients", "has initial dose", "has initial dose for extended release suspension", "has initial dose for pediatric patients", "has maintenance dose", "has maximum dose", "has maximum dose for extended release suspension", "has maximum dose for pediatric patients"]
Answer:

completion:
has initial dose: The subject drug is started at the dose amount and administration schedule specified by the object entity.  
has dose titration: The subject drug's dose is gradually increased according to the schedule specified by the object entity.  
has maintenance dose: The subject drug is taken at the specified daily dose in divided amounts for ongoing treatment.  
has maximum dose: The highest recommended daily dose of the subject drug is specified by the object entity.  
has alternative dosing for doses above 2000 mg: When the subject drug dose exceeds 2000 mg, it should be administered according to the alternative schedule specified by the object entity.  
has daily dose for pediatric patients: For pediatric patients, the subject drug is taken at the specified daily amount as outlined by the object entity.  
has initial dose for pediatric patients: The subject drug is initiated in pediatric patients at the dose and schedule specified by the object entity.  
has initial dose for extended release suspension: The subject drug in extended-release suspension is started at the dose and administration schedule specified by the object entity.  
has maximum dose for extended release suspension: The highest recommended daily dose for the extended-release suspension form of the subject drug is specified by the object entity.  
has maximum dose for pediatric patients: The highest recommended daily dose for the subject drug in pediatric patients is specified by the object entity.
